title: Lessons for the aid sector | USAID | The Guardian
description: Letters: USAID’s closure was abrupt, but no PR campaign will bring it back, says Monica Kappiantari
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Letters: USAID’s closure was abrupt, but no PR campaign will bring it back, says Monica Kappiantari
Content: People protest outside the US Capitol in 2025 against Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s plan to shutdown USAID.Photograph: Jim Watson/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPeople protest outside the US Capitol in 2025 against Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s plan to shutdown USAID.Photograph: Jim Watson/AFP/Getty ImagesUSAIDLettersLessons for the aid sectorUSAID’s closure was abrupt, but no PR campaign will bring it back, saysMonica KappiantariSun 6 Sep 2026 12.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 12.37 EDTShareJeremiah A Carew argues that USAID fell because of poor storytelling rather than poor work (How misconceptions and woeful PR allowed Musk to shred USAID so easily, 1 September). Having spent decades in a recipient nation working at the final point of delivery, I see a different lesson. The primary problem was not the story USAID told, but the architecture behind it.Aid money passes through a heavy supply chain: from prime contractors down through international and local NGOs, with administrative costs absorbed at every layer. Meanwhile, project success is too often measured by easy outputs, such as workshop attendance, rather than long-term systemic impact. There is also a quiet truth: aid workers, including local consultants like myself, often benefit when projects extend, creating incentives to prolong processes rather than complete them.ComparingUSAIDto Nasa is equally unhelpful. Nasa delivers visible, binary moments of engineering triumph. Aid involves slow, complex and contested social change shaped by local politics. No amount of polished marketing can package that like a rocket launch.USAID’s closure was abrupt, but no PR campaign will bring it back. The real lesson for the broader aid sector is to focus less on telling a better story and more on structural reform: shortening the supply chain and funding local actors directly, as some Nordic donors already do, measuring genuine outcomes, and rewarding work that truly finishes.Monica KappiantariDevelopment specialist, Jakarta, IndonesiaExplore more on these topicsUSAIDAidTrump administrationNasalettersShareReuse this content

title: Therapists should never play God in people’s lives | Counselling and therapy | The Guardian
description: Letters: Karin Blak responds to an article by Nicholas Purcell, in which the relationship psychotherapist said he sometimes advises couples to end their marriages
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Letters: Karin Blak responds to an article by Nicholas Purcell, in which the relationship psychotherapist said he sometimes advises couples to end their marriages
Content: ‘If we begin to regard ourselves as knowing which marriages should live and which should die, we risk replacing our clients’ judgment with our own.’Photograph: Science Photo Library/AlamyView image in fullscreen‘If we begin to regard ourselves as knowing which marriages should live and which should die, we risk replacing our clients’ judgment with our own.’Photograph: Science Photo Library/AlamyCounselling and therapyLettersTherapists should never play God in people’s livesKarin Blakresponds to an article by Nicholas Purcell, in which the relationship psychotherapist said he sometimes advises couples to end their marriagesSun 6 Sep 2026 12.34 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 12.35 EDTShareNicholas Purcell’s article concerns me greatly, not because he recognises that some relationships are abusive and dangerous, but because he appears to place the decision about whether a relationship should “die” in the hands of the therapist (As a therapist, here’s why I sometimes advise couples to end their marriage, 31 August).As a psychosexual and relationship therapist, I would never presume to know whether a client should leave their relationship. Our role is not to make that decision for them but to help clients understand what is happening within their relationship, explore patterns of behaviour and coping strategies, recognise coercion or abuse where it exists, consider the options available to them, and understand the possible consequences of those choices.Where abuse is present, couples therapy may be entirely inappropriate. We may need to talk explicitly about risk, a safety plan, involve specialist services and support a client through separation if that is whattheydecide. But the decision remains theirs, not the therapist’s.That distinction matters because of the considerable power the client invests in therapists, who often come to us at their most vulnerable. If we begin to regard ourselves as knowing which marriages should live and which should die, we risk replacing our clients’ judgment with our own.Indeed, in relationships where someone’s sense of self has been diminished through coercion or control, one of therapy’s important functions can be to help restore agency. It would be a troubling tragedy if, in attempting to free a client from someone else’s certainty about what is best for them, the therapist substituted their own.Karin BlakPsychosexual and relationship therapist; author of The Essential Companion to Talking TherapyExplore more on these topicsCounselling and therapyMarriageRelationshipsFamilylettersShareReuse this content

title: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea
Content: Arsenal's manager, Mikel Arteta, makes his point to his captain, Martin Ødegaard during their win over Chelsea.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APView image in fullscreenArsenal's manager, Mikel Arteta, makes his point to his captain, Martin Ødegaard during their win over Chelsea.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APArsenal‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to comeManager delighted by reaction to Chelsea’s openerAlonso says his side must be ‘tighter’Jacob Steinbergat the Emirates StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 15.52 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 18.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after thePremier Leaguechampions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday.Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season whenMorgan Rogersstruck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over ChelseaRead more“It was an exceptional performance,” Arteta said. “I enjoyed every minute from beginning to end, and the beginning was tough. But the team responded in a spectacular way – the conviction, the determination, the quality. It was beautiful. It was a fascinating game.“I think it’s an indication for us of how we are capable of ­performing at an even higher level than last ­season. It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team. We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer. This is the ambition of the team.”Arsenal and City are the only sides who have won their first three games, a statistic Arteta took as evidence that the league will be even harder this time. “It is going to be super hard, the margins you win games,” he said.“We went to Villa Park a few days ago and it was really tough. Today again. We’ll go to Sunderland and it’ll again be so, so tough. We know every week is going to be like this but that’s what we prepare for.”Arteta was delighted with an exceptional midfield display from Ødegaard. Arsenal’s captain looks fit after two years of injury problems and has started the campaign with three goals in four games.“He feels, confidence-wise, I think one of the highest that I’ve seen him,” Arteta said of the Norwegian. “He has a point to prove from last season as well, missing so much football. Kai is the same. I don’t know how many times they played together in the last three years but probably not much. He is enjoying his football. He was running ­forward, having shots, creating for his teammates.”Arteta, who hopes Cristhian ­Mosquera will make a swift recovery from a muscle problem, was similarly positive about Havertz after the ­German impressed against his old club. “He looks settled, he looks happy, in his personal life some great things have happened,” he said. “He looks fit, he looks happy and he is scoring goals.”View image in fullscreenKai Havertz (right) celebrates scoring Arsenal’s first goal with Christos Tzolis and Gabriel.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersWhile Arsenal celebrated, ­Chelsea reflected on coming up short. The Blues were exciting in attack but defensive shortcomings led to their first defeat underXabi Alonso, whose new team have conceded seven in their first three league games.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“My priority is to win games and it’s easier when you don’t concede many,” Alonso said. “This is something that we need to address. We want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.“We wanted to compete, we came to win. We were not that far, but it went their way. We could have scored to make it 2-1 and you never know what happens. But the result is the result, I’m not fighting against that. It hurts. But this is the first defeat, it is going to be a long journey and it doesn’t have a big impact in our mood.”Chelsea are without a clean sheet in their past 19 league games but Alonso did not want to park the bus. “I want to compete in the best possible way to win,” he said. “Today we didn’t want to sit deep from the first minute and to wait and to make a long game. We wanted to be active, we wanted to be protagonists in the pressing, sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower, to have good possessions. And we have done many right things. We need to make it better.”Alonso was optimistic that Moisés Caicedo is not enduring a long-term issue after the midfielder missed out with injury. Caicedo is yet to start this season and it is uncertain if he will be back for Chelsea’s Carabao Cup tie against Leeds on Wednesday.“It’s about assessing the risk,” Alonso said. “Probably last week we took him on too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalMikel ArtetaChelseaXabi AlonsoPremier LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Carlos Alcaraz takes it up a level as he reaches US Open quarter-final | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: The reigning champion beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to move into the last eight at Flushing Meadows
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: The reigning champion beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to move into the last eight at Flushing Meadows
Content: Carlos Alcaraz said Flushing Meadows was special to him.Photograph: Cristóbal Herrera/EPAView image in fullscreenCarlos Alcaraz said Flushing Meadows was special to him.Photograph: Cristóbal Herrera/EPAUS Open Tennis 2026Carlos Alcaraz takes it up a level as he reaches US Open quarter-finalReigning champion beats Tommy Paul in straight setsSabalenka and Noskova to clash in last eightTumaini Carayolat Flushing MeadowsSun 6 Sep 2026 16.16 EDTFirst published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 16.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe straightforward scoreline at the end of Carlos Alcaraz’s third-round win over Wu Yibing did not quite reflect the Spaniard’s slight irritation with one aspect of his game. Alcaraz felt he had missed a few too many forehands, and almost immediately after departing Arthur Ashe Stadium, he reappeared on the practice court pounding forehands in the afternoon heat.Two days later, the extra care Alcaraz put into his game was reflected in a statement performance driven by his peerless forehand as he rose to the occasion in the biggest challenge of his comeback so far, dismantling the 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to continue his title defence by returning to the quarter-finals of the US Open.Dane Sweeny’s ‘career-changing’ US Open comes to an end – along with Australia’s singles hopesRead moreComing into the fourth round, things had progressed about as well as Alcaraz could have hoped. He had been efficient, clean and, most of all, he was striking the ball with total freedom after months of being unable to even use his wrist. The level the 23-year-old displayed on Sunday and the ease with which he dispatched such a high-quality opponent in Paul, however, took him to another level in his comeback.Afterwards, Paul spoke candidly about how vast the gap felt between himself and the seven-time grand slam champion. “It sucks, you know?” he said. “It felt like he’s playing at a completely different level than me, which is, like I said in the beginning, I could have played a lot better and still lost that match.“I was talking to my team right after the match. It sucks, because you feel like, ‘shit, it’s tough to win these matches against him.’ But at the same time, you learn a lot every time you play him.”There was plenty of doubt surrounding Alcaraz’s readiness to compete for the title considering he was returning at a major event in the best-of-five-sets format after a four-and-a-half-month layoff due to his wrist injury.His level serves as a message to the rest of the field that will not go unheard, one that he also shared in his on-court interview: “Except one year since 2021, I made at least the quarter-finals here,” Alcaraz said. “That means how special this place is to me, how good I’m playing every time I come here. I’m just trying to enjoy my time on the court.“So it probably doesn’t matter that I was out for four months and a half. Every time that I come here, I play my best.”Despite how well things had progressed, Alcaraz has had some creases to iron out in his game after so much time away.He started the tournament struggling with his serve, which was slower, inconsistent and imprecise. His serve has improved with each round in speed and precision.Considering the standards he has set for so much of his young career, it is hard to imagine that rate of improvement will not continue as the tournament endures.“Carlos is different, I guess,” said Paul. “It’s impressive to take time off like that and come back and feel, play as good as he has. I wouldn’t be able to do it, for sure.”Meanwhile, Aryna Sabalenka’s title defence at the US Open continued to gather steam as she returned to the quarter-finals with a solid performance and an assured victory, defeating Taylor Townsend of the United States 6-4, 6-3.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis was a challenging match despite the routine scoreline, with Sabalenka initially failing to serve out the first set, trailing 1-3 in set two and dropping serve four times.View image in fullscreenAryna Sabalenka will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the quarter-final.Photograph: Heather Khalifa/APHowever, she handled the decisive moments well, rolling through the final five games of the match to advance.“I love matches like that, because it was really challenging, and going through tough challenges and overcoming those challenges, it definitely gives you strength and really strong belief that you can do it,” said Sabalenka. “So these kind of matches is really like a boost of confidence.”A far greater challenge awaits Sabalenka in the quarter-final as she faces the Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova, who appears to be finding her feet again as she continues to digest her life-changing triumph in July.Noskova held her nerve at the end of one of the most spectacular contests of the tournament, recovering after squandering double match point at 5-4 in set two before clinching her sixth match point to close out against the 11th seed, Marta Kostyuk, 7-5, 5-7, 6-4.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026Carlos AlcarazAryna SabalenkaUS Open tennisTennisUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lewis Hamilton rules out world title challenge after Italian Grand Prix setback | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The Briton, who could only finish sixth at Monza after a clash with teammate Charles Leclerc, questioned the strategy of Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The Briton, who could only finish sixth at Monza after a clash with teammate Charles Leclerc, questioned the strategy of Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur
Content: Lewis Hamilton said of Ferrari’s strategy: ‘If we continue to travel the same path, we’ll get the same result.’Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenLewis Hamilton said of Ferrari’s strategy: ‘If we continue to travel the same path, we’ll get the same result.’Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAFormula One 2026Lewis Hamilton rules out world title challenge after Italian Grand Prix setbackBriton finishes sixth after clash with teammate LeclercHamilton questions Ferrari chief Fred Vasseur’s strategyGiles Richardsat MonzaSun 6 Sep 2026 16.16 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLewis Hamilton has conceded theFormula Oneworld ­championship this year is all but out of reach after a bruising Italian Grand Prix. ­Hamilton’s afternoon included a clash with his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc, which he thought was the result of the team’s failure to listen to his entreaties to manage their drivers and execute races better.The race at Monza waswon by Kimi Antonelliafter a remarkable comeback by the Mercedes driver from 19th on the grid. Hamilton could manage only sixth. Having been 59 points back he now trails Antonelli by 76 with 10 meetings remaining and he felt that Ferrari not ­prioritising his title chances, coupled with operational failures, had finally cost him a shot at the drivers’ championship.Antonelli ends Italy’s 60-year wait for home F1 win with Monza triumph from 19thRead more“From today, we’ve just lost so much ground to them on points. It’s far too late for those decisions to come,” he said of giving him priority over Leclerc. “It’s many, many weeks too late. All I can do is just try and turn up. I’ll get up tomorrow morning and I’ll give it my best. I don’t know how many points it is now but it’s an amount and with the pace that they [Mercedes] have, it is a very, very difficult amount to close up.”Leclerc did not finish the race after a huge crash on lap two from which he emerged unhurt. Before that on the first lap at the first ­chicane, Hamilton looked to go past his teammate but was squeezed wide, went off and dropped to 10th place.The seven‑time champion said imme­diately that Leclerc had driven him off track and noted pointedly that the incident demonstrated where Ferrari had been going wrong and that the team principal, Fred ­Vasseur, had to bear responsibility.“Look I don’t race dirty, I have always raced clean and fairly and always left space, so I don’t think they should be worried about me,” he said. “I’ve come into the team and tried to be respectful of space but ultimately it comes from the top. It trickles down. So it starts with Fred and there’s only so much you can say and push and shout from the mountaintop.Quick GuideItalian F1 GP resultsShow1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes1:51:15.281 –25pts2George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes+3.875 –18pts3Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull+14.718 –15pts4Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren+19.056 –12pts5Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren+19.253 –10pts6Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari+24.655 –8pts7Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine+27.351 –6pts8Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls+45.136 –4pts9Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine+47.353 –2pts10Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls+58.187–1pt11Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi+65.18712Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi+66.18713Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams+74.11714Liam Lawson🇳🇿Red Bull+75.60915Oliver Bearman🇬🇧Haas+78.95816Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas+1 lap17Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams+1 lap18Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac+1 lap19Valtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac+2 lapsNCLance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinDNFNCFernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston MartinDNFNCCharles Leclerc🇲🇨FerrariDNFWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“I’ve already said that we had to look at how we communicate because if we continue to travel the same path, we’ll get the same result.”Leclerc is now 112 points behind Antonelli and Vasseur intimated that the team would now consider ­prioritising Hamilton.“The outcome of [turns] one-two is not good for the team,” Vasseur said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If we have a team order or ­whatever? I think that the good comparison that I made was that last year, [Oscar] Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season and if McLaren had put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion.“At one stage you have to take a decision but I think it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Now, we have time to discuss with the guys.”The discussion will have to be swift with the next round in Madrid next weekend but Hamilton was emphatic that Ferrari had to address the issues and once more compared the ­Scuderia’s operational activities unfavourably with his former team, the championship leaders Mercedes.“When I was at Mercedes we had written rules of engagement. And we never really had it too bad,” he said. “There was a moment with me and Nico [­Rosberg] a couple of times but more often than not, it was good. Here there are no rules. That’s something that needs to probably change.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tim Wellens pulls away on last stage to win Tour of Britain | Tour of Britain | The Guardian
description: The Belgian rider Tim Wellens clinched overall victory in the Tour of Britain with the home rider Lewis Askey in second place
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: The Belgian rider Tim Wellens clinched overall victory in the Tour of Britain with the home rider Lewis Askey in second place
Content: Tim Wellens approaches the finish line in the Tour of Britain’s final stage at Earlston.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PAView image in fullscreenTim Wellens approaches the finish line in the Tour of Britain’s final stage at Earlston.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PATour of BritainTim Wellens pulls away on last stage to win Tour of BritainBelgian beats Briton Lewis Askey into secondBradley Wiggins’ son Ben finishes in 10thJeremy WhittleSun 6 Sep 2026 12.55 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTim Wellens, teammate to Tadej Pogacar at the UAE Emirates XRG team, took overall victory in the men’sTour of Britain, after the Belgian rider had decisively snatched the overall race lead on the fourth stage on Saturday, through the hills of North Yorkshire.Wellens had started the final stage in Earlston 21 seconds ahead of Lewis Askey but extended that advantage to 42sec by the finish. The British rider finished second overall after riding impressively through the earlier stages, while Ben Wiggins, the 21-year-old son of Sir Bradley Wiggins, placed 10th overall.Vuelta a España: Marco Brenner wins stage 14 but extreme heat forces shorter stage 15Read moreThe Belgian rider’s German teammate, Nils Politt, took a rare win in the final stage on Sunday, as Pogacar’s team celebrated another well-executed overall victory after a select group, which included five of their riders, broke clear of the peloton in the Lammermuir hills.“It was a very successful week,” Wellens said. “We came here for the GC and today we also have this stage victory, so everything’s been perfect.”The 165-kilometre stage on Saturday from Helmsley to Leyburn was won by Cees Bol of the Netherlands, but the Tour de France stage winner Wellens did enough on the short sharp climbs of the Yorkshire Dales and North York Moors, to distance the overnight leader Askey and take what proved to be an unassailable lead.“Today we just wanted to defend the leader’s jersey,” Wellens said of the final stage through the Scottish Borders. “We didn’t want to attack, we didn’t want to make a hard race, we just wanted to ride defensively. But then suddenly, in the crosswinds Netcompany Ineos started to ride very hard, so we just followed.”View image in fullscreenNils Politt shows his delight at winning the final stage.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PAThe British team, whose hopes were frustrated once again by inopportune punctures earlier in the race, took the initiative on the windswept moors, in an attempt to crack UAE Emirates XRG’s hold on the overall standings, but race leader Wellens was well protected and never really looked at risk.Politt’s stage-winning move from a leading group that included Wiggins, came with less than 10km remaining. A race that began with a tribute from the peloton to Fin Tarling,who died last monthin the Volta a Portugal, ended with another poignant moment as Politt pointed to the sky when he crossed the finish line in memory of his grandfather.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe repercussions of Tarling’s death in August continue to be felt across the sport and recent further lapses in race security, including at both the women’s and men’s Tour of Britain, have only intensified the debate.In response the sport’s governing body, the UCI, has now stressed the “urgent need to put in place, as quickly as possible, a dedicated safety system allowing the real-time location of riders and vehicles to be tracked at all professional road cycling events, starting with those in the UCI WorldTour and UCI Women’s WorldTour”.Explore more on these topicsTour of BritainCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw | Everton | The Guardian
description: The manager, praising Everton’s resilience after securing a late 2-2 draw with Manchester United, said: ‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: The manager, praising Everton’s resilience after securing a late 2-2 draw with Manchester United, said: ‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’
Content: David Moyes said Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester United was a ‘brilliant goal, brilliant technique’.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAView image in fullscreenDavid Moyes said Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester United was a ‘brilliant goal, brilliant technique’.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAEverton‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United drawManager praises team’s resilience after late equaliser‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’Andy Hunterat Hill Dickinson StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 14.49 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 15.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDavid Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind tosalvage a point against Manchester Unitedthrough Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.Maitland-Niles stunner rescues late point for Everton against Manchester UnitedRead moreTyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If nobody knew you that goal would get you plenty of headlines,” he said of Maitland-Niles, a £4.3m deadline-day signing from Lyon. “It was a brilliant goal, brilliant technique. title: Sophia Dunkley’s 119 guides England to 3-0 win over Ireland despite batting collapse | Women's cricket | The Guardian
description: A fine hundred from Sophia Dunkley ensured England sealed a series clean sweep in their third ODI against Ireland at Worcester on Sunday, but not before a disappointing batting collapse
Author: Raf Nicholson
Headline: A fine hundred from Sophia Dunkley ensured England sealed a series clean sweep in their third ODI against Ireland at Worcester on Sunday, but not before a disappointing batting collapse
Content: Sophia Dunkley hits out on her way to a match-defining century.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenSophia Dunkley hits out on her way to a match-defining century.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersWomen's cricketSophia Dunkley’s 119 guides England to 3-0 win over Ireland despite batting collapseBatter hits second ODI century of career to set up victoryIreland capture England’s final six wickets for 31 runsRaf Nicholsonat WorcesterSun 6 Sep 2026 13.01 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 19.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA fine hundred from Sophia Dunkley ensured England sealed a series clean sweep in their third one-day international against Ireland at Worcester on Sunday, but not before a disappointing batting collapse.The hosts, batting first for the first time in the series, had looked on course for a huge total after Dunkley’s and Maia Bouchier’s powerful ball‑striking up top. But the innings finished limply with the loss of their last six wickets for 31 runs, as England were bowled out for 291 in 48.5 overs.England win third women’s ODI against Ireland to complete series sweep – as it happenedRead moreIn reply Ireland got off to a flyer thanks to their captain, Gaby Lewis, who struck the ball so forcefully out of the ground on to the concrete concourse that the umpires had to call for a replacement. But when Lewis top‑edged a bouncer from Lauren Filer out into the deep, the required run rate quickly became too much of a mountain to climb.Charlotte Edwards, the England head coach, said: “We came into this series with the intention and the goal of beating Ireland 3-0 and we’ve done that so I’m really pleased. We’ve obviously managed to develop a few players and give some opportunities throughout, so it feels like a really positive end to the summer.”Edwards also seemed satisfied with the results of her experiment involving Alice Capsey as keeper. Capsey added two stumpings on Sunday to her glovework highlights reel – the second a very decent effort standing up to a Ryana MacDonald-Gay bouncer, as Ireland subsided to 177 all out.“The idea of this was to see where she’s at,” Edwards said. “There’s a real chance [for her to keep] in T20 cricket. We want competition for places and she’s certainly put her hand up in that department.”Nevertheless, there remains something of a winter headache for Edwards as she tries to figure out how to turn this new-look side into an Ashes-winning side.Neither of England’s two young picks – the 21-year-old left-hander Jodi Grewcock and the 19-year-old Tilly Corteen-Coleman – have yet made a decisive contribution. Grewcock, given a run in the No 3 role this series, contributed 35 runs on Sunday but also faced 26 balls before striking her first boundary. The left-arm spinner Corteen-Coleman finally extracted some turn from the Worcester pitch, outwitting Alice Tector and dislodging the stumps of Louise Little, but she remains well behind Sophie Ecclestone and Linsey Smith in the pecking order.Earlier, Lewis had called correctly at the toss while she also broke some surprising news: the retirement of the all-rounder Arlene Kelly from international cricket. Kelly, who grew up in New Zealand, was playing domestic cricket in Ireland in 2022 when she received a shock call-up from then coach Ed Joyce: since then, she has represented her adopted nation 110 times and taken 136 wickets. She has now decided the time is right to return to New Zealand.Handed the new ball in her final ODI, Kelly added a single wicket to her collection – MacDonald-Gay holing out to long-on in the 48th over. Instead, it was the leg-spinner Cara Murray who had a day to remember, finishing with four for 56.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGrewcock plonked a return catch back to the leg-spinner, Freya Kemp and Mady Villiers were caught in the deep, and Murray also turned one past the bat of Charlie Dean and took her edge.Dunkley’s second ODI hundred – her first since 2022 – proved England’s salvation. The right-hander missed the early summer ODIs against New Zealand to manage her workload but this series has proved her mettle as an ODI opener, muscling her way to 73 in the first match and showcasing her 360-degree ability here with powerful punches down the ground and some nifty scoops behind square.England can now rest and regroup before a busy February which will involve a bilateral series against Sri Lanka and the Champions Trophy tournament in India.Explore more on these topicsWomen's cricketEngland women's cricket teamIreland women's cricket teamCricketmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning start | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Khadija Shaw scored twice as Manchester City began the defence of the Women’s Super League title with a 3-1 win against Birmingham
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Khadija Shaw scored twice as Manchester City began the defence of the Women’s Super League title with a 3-1 win against Birmingham
Content: Khadija Shaw shows her delight after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw shows her delight after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWomen’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning startStriker scores twice to sink BirminghamArsenal, Palace, Spurs and Liverpool winTom Garryat the Joie StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 14.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSome things just feel inevitable. Some strikers just feel inevitable. Despite a new season, a fresh start and new opponents, it is still the same storyline forManchester City: Khadija Shaw wins them the game. The Jamaica striker began the campaign exactly how she finished the previous league season, with two goals, and demonstrated why it was so crucial that the club eventually persuaded her to sign a new contract in the summer.Last season’s Golden Boot winner in the Women’s Super League could have scored at least twice in the first half had it not been for an excellent debut performance from Sophie Baggaley in goal for promotedBirmingham.Brighton 0-1 Arsenal: Women’s Super League – as it happenedRead moreShaw, though, was not to be denied and she rose highest to head in twice from second-half corners, taken first by Kerstin Casparij and then by the debutant Beth Mead, to score her side’s second and third goals in a 3-1 victory. By then, Mary Fowler’s low finish had already opened the scoring with Manchester City’s 1,000th goal as a professional women’s side.Birmingham grabbed a late consolation goal through Océane Hurtré, who capitalised on a defensive lapse from Jade Rose and rolled the ball home in the 90th minute, and there were plenty of encouraging signs overall for the second-tier champions of last season.Quick GuidePalace face scrutiny over substitutionsShowCrystal Palace could face a points deduction or potentially be forced to replay their game against Everton on Sunday, which Palace won 1-0, after it emerged that the hosts breached the rules around substitutions by making changes at four separate moments in the second half of the Women's Super League match.The WSL, Pro Ref and both clubs have all launched investigations into the incident. The newly promoted Palace brought on Kirsty Howat to replace Shannon O'Brien in the 97th minute, having already made three previous substitutions across three separate second-half opportunities.A WSL spokesperson said: "We can confirm there was a breach of competition rules in the Crystal Palace versus Everton match. Crystal Palace used a fourth substitution opportunity during a fourth stoppage in play, when the rules permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match. We will now conduct an investigation alongside both clubs and Pro Ref and update in due course."Jo Potter's side were already leading the match thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith's 34th-minute opener. There were eight minutes of stoppage time indicated for the end of the second half, so the  substitution in question came with merely seconds remaining. The consequences could be significant for Palace, depending on the outcome of the investigation and the verdict of any potential tribunal.The WSL's rules regarding the fielding of an ineligible player list the potential punishments in rule 7.13.2, which include the possibility that the points gained from the match be deducted or that the match be replayed. It is understood that the team of match officials who worked on that Palace-Everton game will not be appointed to the next round of games in WSL/ WSL2 on the weekend of 12-13 September, in light of this incident.Teams are permitted to use no more than three substitution opportunities per match, in addition to being able to make replacements at half-time and for concussion substitutions.Tom GarryWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The Blues were playing on the same ground where they were relegated in 2022 after a 6-0 loss to City, but on Sunday Amy Merricks’s side look far more competitive than the Birmingham team that said goodbye to the top tier four seasons ago, having kept the scoreline goalless until after half-time.Nonetheless, on the day of Lauren Hemp’s 200th City appearance it was a dominant start from the defending champions, whose head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, said: “We created a lot of scoring chances. The first half [we were] a little bit hesitant on the ball, not determined with or without the ball, but the second half was better.”View image in fullscreenArsenal’s Lisa Baum fires in the only goal at Brighton.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersMerricks, who hailed Baggaley’s debut as “exceptional”, said: “We got into some good areas and lacked just a bit of anticipation that we would get there. That’s just down to belief, that’s not quality. I’m really pleased with the performance. I’m disappointed with the result but really pleased with the platform we’ve given ourselves to build on.”Earlier, Lisa Baum marked herArsenaldebut with an exquisitely taken goal and her early strike was enough to secure a 1-0 victory atBrightonand inflict a defeat on their new head coach, Arturo Ruiz. The 19‑year‑old Germany youth international created room to shoot inside the area in the 10th minute and rifled home a clinical finish from a tight angle, in off the underside of the crossbar, to make an immediate impression on the delighted, travelling Arsenal fans behind that goal.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBaum, who arrived this summer from RB Leipzig, was one of four new signings to start the game for Arsenal, alongside Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez. Arsenal had failed to win at Brighton in the past two league campaigns and will have been very satisfied to open their title bid with a victory as they seek to hunt down a first league title since 2019. Ruiz, who has been in charge at Brighton for nine days, saw some encouraging signs from his new team with Kiko Seike and Fran Kirby both going close.It was a day for important debut goals as Lexi Lloyd-Smith slotted home on her first appearance forCrystal Palaceto give the promoted side a priceless 1-0 win againstEvertonto start their campaign. Another debutant quickly impressed atTottenhamas their new striker Kirsty Hanson scored twice to help them to beatWest Ham3-1.Liverpoolwere the day’s most emphatic winners as they cruised to a 4-0 win at promotedCharlton. The Germany striker Vivien Endemann scored on her debut for Liverpool after Grace Fisk had scored twice. Cornelia Kapocs added a stoppage‑time penalty to make it a poor start for Charlton, who did not register a shot on target and recorded just two efforts off target.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester City WomenBirmingham City WomenArsenal WomenWomen's footballBrighton & Hove Albion WomenCrystal Palace WomennewsShareReuse this content

title: Richard Hughes confirmed as Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool departure | Al-Hilal | The Guardian
description: The former Liverpool sporting director has taken up the position at Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The former Liverpool sporting director has taken up the position at Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia
Content: Richard Hughes (centre) will work with Al-Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenRichard Hughes (centre) will work with Al-Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAAl-HilalRichard Hughes confirmed as Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool departureHughes joins Saudi exodus after two years at AnfieldMartinelli, Summerville and Watkins are at Al-HilalReuters and Guardian sportSun 6 Sep 2026 17.15 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 17.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRichard Hughes has been appointed as the sporting director ⁠of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club confirmed on ⁠Sunday, following ⁠his ​departure from Liverpool.Hughes, 47, joinedLiverpoolin 2024 from Bournemouth. ⁠He appointed Arne Slot as Jürgen Klopp’s successor as head coach, ⁠a decision that paid immediate dividends ​as the Reds ‌claimed the ‌Premier League title in 2024-25. Slot ‌was sacked and replaced by Andoni Iraola in June.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLiverpool look for new sporting director after Richard Hughes formally leavesRead more“The appointment of Hughes came as part of Al-Hilal’s efforts to strengthen its football system ‌and develop its sporting structure with specialised expertise,” the Saudi Pro League leaders ​said in a statement.The appointment highlights Al-Hilal’s drive to tap into English football, with Hughes the latest ⁠former Premier League figure to join ​the ​Riyadh-based club. Hughes follows playersGabriel ​Martinelli, Crysencio Summerville and ​Ollie Watkins, ‌who joined ​the ​Saudi club this summer from Arsenal, West Ham United and Aston Villa, respectively. Al-Hilal’s manager is Simone Inzaghi, formerly of Inter.Two members of Liverpool’s recruitment department are set to follow Hughes to Al Hilal. Mark Burchill and Craig McKee, who joined Liverpool from Bournemouth with Hughes two years ago, are now poised to team up with the Scot in Saudi.Explore more on these topicsAl-HilalLiverpoolnewsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia | European club football | The Guardian
description: Fermín, Raphinha and Pedri also score to keep 100% record
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Fermín, Raphinha and Pedri also score to keep 100% record
Content: Lamine Yamal silences the Mestalla by giving Barcelona the lead after only six minutes.Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLamine Yamal silences the Mestalla by giving Barcelona the lead after only six minutes.Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesEuropean club footballEuropean football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of ValenciaGatti’s stoppage-time header rescues Juve against MilanGoalkeeper Koeman Jr scores two penalties in EredivisieAgenciesSun 6 Sep 2026 17.25 EDTFirst published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 14.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLamine Yamal struck twice forBarcelonaas they demolishedValencia5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’sReal Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betison Friday. Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.European football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten InterRead moreBarcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Fermín dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star. Fermín netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after the former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up. Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric García had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with teammate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start sincearriving this summer from Manchester City.Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Fermín fed him. The Valencia goalkeeper, Stole Dimitrievski, saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo. Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barça debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide. Lamine Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barça’s fifth.In Serie A, Ruben Amorim’sMilanwere pegged back by a 92nd-minute equaliser fromJuventusin a 1-1 draw in Turin on Sunday. Teenage sensation Alphadjo Cisse had given Milan the lead but the Juve centre-back Federico Gatti came off the bench to head home and earn a share of the spoils in stoppage time.Milan took the lead on 69 minutes ⁠with a superb finish from Cisse, who controlled Samuel Chukwueze’s crossfield pass with a deft touch in the box. The 19-year-old showed quick feet to create space to shoot ⁠and fired the ball low into the far corner, adding to his debut goal away ​at Torino on the opening day. But the visitors could not ‌hold on and when Teun Koopmeiners delivered a cross from the left, Gatti rose highest to score ‌with a powerful header.View image in fullscreenJuventus’s Federico Gatti takes the acclaim of the Turin crowd after levelling against Milan at the death.Photograph: Marco Alpozzi/LaPresse/APThe ⁠draw leaves both sides ⁠on seven points ​from their opening three games, with Milan fourth on the table, ahead of fifth-placed Juve on goals scored.Giorgi Kvernadze scored a winner seven minutes from the end to secure all three points forFrosinoneat home toVeneziaafter the latter had rallied from two goals down but went home with nothing.Bolognatwice came from behind to secure a 2-2 draw at home toSassuolo, a game that ended with the hosts’ head coach Domenico Tedesco receiving a red card. Artem Dovbyk netted his first goal for the ​home side to equalise in stoppage time.The English 19-year-old Jay Robinson gaveMonzaa 1-0 lead in the first half atParma, but 18-year-old Simone Lontani equalised on the hour-mark, with the game finishing 1-1. For both players it was their firstSerie Agoals, and for both clubs their first point of the campaign. Forward Robinson is on loan at Monza from Southampton.Meanwhile, Ronald Koeman Jr, the goalkeeper son of the former Netherlands player and manager Ronald Koeman, scored two penalties for Dutch sideTelstarto rescue a point in theirEredivisiematch withCambuur. His second spot-kick was converted in the 11th minute of added time.Koeman Jr, 31, converted his first penalty on 63 minutes before his ice-cool equaliser. He previously scored from the spot at the end of last season to ensure his side avoided relegation from the Dutch top flight.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenTelstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr is hugged by a teammate after his late penalty rescued a point.Photograph: ANP/ShutterstockIn Germany,Mainzignited their Bundesliga season with a thumping 5-0 win over haplessHamburg, whileAugsburgclimbed ⁠to the top of the table following a 4-1 win atEintracht Frankfurton Sunday.Mainz took the lead on 19 minutes as Sheraldo Becker was played in on goal by ⁠Kaishu Sano and picked out the bottom corner. Becker then turned provider as his low cross was converted at the back post by Phillipp Mwene for ⁠a 2-0 half-time lead.Becker was again involved with the next goal as he set up ​Phillip Tietz to bundle the ball home. Tietz ‌then added a fourth ‌as he beat Heuer Fernandes, before Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer punished his former employers ‌with a fifth.Augsburg have a haul of six points following ​their excellent win at Frankfurt, where they had to come from behind, having trailed 1-0 at half-time. Jonathan Burkardt headed the home side in front inside six minutes.Arijon Ibrahimovic ​headed in at the back post ​on debut inside the first minute of the re-start for the equaliser. Within a minute, ‌Augsburg were 2-1 ahead ​as the ball ​fell to Robin Fellhauer in the box and he converted to turn the game on its head. Alexis Claude-Maurice and Fabian Rieder added further goalsAugsburg lead theBundesligaon goal difference ahead of Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and Elversberg, who all have two wins from two.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballBarcelonaValenciaLa LigaAugsburgMainz 05HamburgnewsShareReuse this content

title: Energy secretary says US might not reach nuclear agreement with Iran | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
description: Chris Wright tells ABC there ‘may not’ be an agreement that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons
Author: Maya Yang
Headline: Chris Wright tells ABC there ‘may not’ be an agreement that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons
Content: The US energy secretary, Chris Wright, in Caracas, Venezuela, on Wednesday.Photograph: Leonardo Fernández Viloria/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe US energy secretary, Chris Wright, in Caracas, Venezuela, on Wednesday.Photograph: Leonardo Fernández Viloria/ReutersUS-Israel war on IranEnergy secretary says US might not reach nuclear agreement with IranChris Wright tells ABC there ‘may not’ be an agreement that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weaponsMaya YangSun 6 Sep 2026 13.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUS energy secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday morning that the US may not be able to reach a nuclear agreement withIranthat would prevent the country from having nuclear weapons.Asked on ABC on Sunday morning about any sign of such a deal, as negotiations appear stalled and theUS-Israel war on Irancontinues, Wright said: “There may not be a nuclear agreement.”He talked about options for ending the “existential threat” of a nuclear armed Iran coming about by further US military action to knock out the country’s capacity to manufacture and deploy such missiles, saying: “It may be simply [a case of] destroying their capabilities to do it” or else “an agreement may await the next administration in Iran”.He later said on CBS that the US was not shutting down diplomatic outreach and was “always open for a deal”. Wright told that network’s Face the Nation show that the “biggest role” of the US military in the Gulf region currently was to stop Iranian energy exports.“We are strangling their economy to try to bring either a change in policy from the existing regime or a new regime,” he said.In an earlier interview with CNN on Sunday, Wright declined to declare thestrait of Hormuzsafe for oil tankers – unless they are being escorted by the US navy – and stopped short of saying whether the navy would need to remain in the Gulf region “indefinitely” in order to keep the vital energy passageway operating, as the conflictdrags on.How the Iran war unfolded: every attack and oil price change – visualisedRead moreThis came despite Donald Trump’s repeated claims that ships can safely navigate the narrow marine waterway, and the US president’sinsistencelast week that the US controls the strait, while floating the idea that it be named after him – statements that were followed byfurther strikesfrom both sides in the area.Wright, appearing for an interview on CNN’s State of the Union show on Sunday as well as ABC and CBS, was asked whether he could “unequivocally” assure safety to merchant ships transiting the strait. The question came after a New York Timesreportfound that August was the deadliest month for merchant vessels in the area since March.“We’re working cooperatively with fleets that do want to transit. Some ships aren’t transiting, and, of course, that’s their choice. But the United States is working with teams from all the nations in the Gulf to get transits and to continue to ramp them up,” Wright said.“But you’re not saying that it’s currently safe?” host CNN Dana Bash asked, to which Wright replied: “We’re getting a lot of ships through, but, of course, it requires the US military to do that. We are not [at] pre-conflict levels, if that’s what you’re asking.”Bash then asked: “If a country or a company wants to send its tanker through the strait of Hormuz, can they do so safely?”“Well, if they want to work with the United States navy, I think they can,” Wright said.Bash then asked whether the US navy would remain in the region “indefinitely” and whether its presence in the strait was becoming “the new normal”.Wright responded: “Well, it is today, but I think, as you look forward, other nations will come and work with us in this endeavor. Certainly, trade for the world is important. It shouldn’t be just the United States’s responsibility.”“But until Iran changes their position or changes their government, we’ll have to deal with them. But, slowly, their capabilities are being degraded and ours are being enhanced,” he added.Iran war likely to drag on for another six months, ex-US defense secretary warnsRead moreNuclear and diplomatic talks between the United States and Iran appear to havestalledafter a June interim agreement to end military operationscollapsedwithout producing a lasting settlement on peace or the future of what remains of Iran’s nuclear program after USstrikes last summercausedhuge damage.Wright was also asked by CNN if he would say the US is still at war. “We’re still in a conflict, for sure,” he said. On Thursday, the US vice-president JD Vancesaidat a White House press briefing: “I wouldn’t call it a war,” instead referring to a military conflict. Trump thendefendedVance, saying: “A lot of people do not call it a war, I would call it a military conflict, because it’s small potatoes for us … it’s not a big thing.”The Republican US senator John Kennedy of Louisiana was asked on Sunday by NBC if the war would be over by November.“Probably not,” he said.The conflict passed the six-month mark in late August. The former defense secretary Leon Panetta warnedin an interviewwith the Guardian this weekend that it could last a lot longer.Explore more on these topicsUS-Israel war on IranUS foreign policyIranTrump administrationMiddle East and north AfricanewsShareReuse this content

title: EU faces 300,000 factory job cuts as China ‘colonises’ supply chains, industry warns | Manufacturing sector | The Guardian
description: Protest using 10 coffins to symbolise struggling manufacturing industry to take place in Brussels
Author: Lisa O’Carroll
Headline: Protest using 10 coffins to symbolise struggling manufacturing industry to take place in Brussels
Content: A steelworker in Germany. In June the EU introduced higher tariffs on imports of foreign steel.Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/ReutersView image in fullscreenA steelworker in Germany. In June the EU introduced higher tariffs on imports of foreign steel.Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/ReutersManufacturing sectorEU faces 300,000 factory job cuts as China ‘colonises’ supply chains, industry warnsProtest using 10 coffins to symbolise struggling manufacturing industry to take place in BrusselsLisa O’CarrollSenior correspondentSun 6 Sep 2026 13.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 15.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJob losses in EU manufacturing will rapidly increase unless Brussels stops the “colonisation” of industry by Chinese component manufacturers, a leading industry trade body has warned.Eurometal predicts 300,000 job losses in manufacturing in the rest of 2026 because of expanding competition from China, which is now enjoying a record€1bn-a-day trade surpluswith the bloc.On Monday, Eurometal will bring its concerns to decision-makers in Brussels, staging a protest using 10 symbolic coffins in a procession around the European Commission headquarters.The coffins will be marked with phrases such as “EU competitiveness”, “industrial jobs” and “European factories”.European manufacturers fear that the commission is not fully alive to thecannibalisation of their industriesas China becomes embedded in supply chains through the sale of components.Alexander Julius, the president of Eurometal, told the Guardian: “China has made no secret of what it is doing. It is in their five-year plan.“China doesn’t want to be a raw material supplier, it wants to be a finished product supply. They want to be in key product supply chains because they know that once they control the supply chain, they own the complete value chain.” He wants the commission to understand fully the impact of Chinese exports at component level, including metals and chemicals used in 90% of manufacturing.The EU has already taken action on electric vehicles by imposing tariffs on Chinese imports in 2024, and in June introduced higher tariffs on imports of foreign steel. The bloc’s trade commissioner, Maroš Šefčovič, has also said the EU’s €360bn (£310bn) annual import/export imbalance with China is “not sustainable”, with both sides agreeing to hold three months of talks, ending in October,to try to avert a trade war.“You look at the job losses stacking up in industries in places like Germany. The media, the politicians can see the consequences, but they don’t go after the virus that is causing it,” Julius said. “They don’t see why it is happening or ask why companies are either relocating to China or India or going bust.”Among the conditions allowing the “virus” to spread is the increasing costs borne by European metal manufacturers with tariffs on steel imports and carbon emissions taxes for those high-energy sectors.Components manufactured in China face none of those levies, said Julius, and that, combined with the undervaluation of the Chinese currency, the yuan, makes it challenging to compete with Chinese rivals, he added.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCompanies have to satisfy shareholders and will continue to buy from China, whatever the political rhetoric coming out of Brussels, he said.“When manufacturing leaves Europe, Europe not only loses production but investment, knowhow and long-term economic resilience,” Eurometal said ahead of the protest.Analysis by the European Commission in June projected potential job losses of more than 1m on the back of high energy costs and global competition, which will include the100,000 job cuts at Volkswagenconfirmed by the German carmaker last week.China has repeatedly accused Europe of protectionism. It threatened “resolute countermeasures should the EU further target Chinese companies or products”, according to the state-owned Xinhua agency earlier this year. Since then, the EU and China have agreed a three-month truce.Explore more on these topicsManufacturing sectorEuropean UnionInternational tradeChinaEuropeJob lossesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Farage says overseas donation row ‘looks bad’ but denies Reform broke law | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
description: Robert Jenrick says party has followed legal protocol ‘at all times’ as Met police consider launching investigation
Author: Pippa Crerar
Headline: Robert Jenrick says party has followed legal protocol ‘at all times’ as Met police consider launching investigation
Content: Nigel Farage’s party has been hit with a fresh financial scandal during its annual party conference.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAView image in fullscreenNigel Farage’s party has been hit with a fresh financial scandal during its annual party conference.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPANigel FarageFarage says overseas donation row ‘looks bad’ but denies Reform broke lawRobert Jenrick says party has followed legal protocol ‘at all times’ as Met police consider launching investigationPippa CrerarPolitical editorSun 6 Sep 2026 07.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 15.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNigel Farage has acknowledged the overseas donation row engulfing Reform UK “looks bad” for his party but denied it had ever taken foreign money in breach of electoral law.The Reform leader, who is battling to contain the fallout from the allegations, was asked if he could categorically rule out that foreign money had ever been funnelled to his party. He replied: “I can. Never happened.”Farage was forced to suspend his close aide Dan Jukes and Reform’s head of policy, James Orr, on Friday after they were filmed in an undercover investigation apparently plotting toget around electoral lawson foreign donations.In an interview with the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg, Farage described their comments as “injudicious at best” and admitted the optics of the undercover filming were problematic for his party, which has in the past tried to suggest it would do politics differently.“This looks bad, as does the sale of peerages, as does government contracts for donations,” he said. “We are not the first people to be involved in a row over donations.”The questions overshadowed the start of Reform’s party conference in Birmingham, where numerous hecklers were removed from the hall during Farage’s keynote speech.Footage has emerged online of one of the women being dragged by her hair, with a man also appearing to hit female protesters with his crutch.When questioned about the incident by Jon Sopel on Sky News’s Sunday Morning programme,Robert Jenricksaid: “Oh, boohoo. We’re now in a country, Jon, where somebody who is – whatever she is – a far-left protester, goes into a party conference, tries to wreck the leader’s speech, and cries foul if a pensioner knocks her over the head with their Zimmer frame.“I mean, come on, get a life,” Reform’s treasury spokesperson added.West Midlands police said they were aware of the footage, adding: “We would ask the woman involved to come forward. Anyone with any information should contact us on 101 quoting log number 924 of 5 September.”After an official complaint that Farage and his aides had broken political funding laws, theMetropolitan policesaid it was assessing the evidence, with sources suggesting a full investigation is expected. They all deny wrongdoing.Scotland Yard could extend an existing investigation into whether Reform took donations channelled through an intermediary from potentially impermissible sources, which the party and donors deny.Farage is already facing intense scrutiny about Reform’s finances, as well as about his£5m giftfrom a crypto billionaire shortly before he announced he would stand in the 2024 general election, which he has since said was intended to pay for security.View image in fullscreenThe Reform MP Robert Jenrick has said a KC reviewed the evidence and found the party had not broken any laws.Photograph: Temilade Adelaja/ReutersIn an earlier extract of the BBC interview, Farage also claimed he“wasn’t even listening”during the meeting at the centre of the controversy, and that he knew donation law “better than anybody”, as he sought to limit the damage caused by the allegations.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionJenrick said on Sunday that he had seen legal advice that the party had not in fact broken electoral law over foreign donations but that lessons would be learned from the episode.“We’re going to investigate exactly what happened,” Jenrick told Sky News. “It’s right to have due process. But this is not the way that Reform conducts itself.“Like any political party, we seek to abide by the law at all times, and we believe we have in this case. In fact, I’ve reviewed the legal advice from the KC who’s advised the party in the last 48 hours, and it shows that, yeah, we did.“But do we want for the best version of ourselves? Yes, absolutely. And no doubt there will be lessons to be learnt from this.”Speaking after the BBC interview, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said: “For a political party that don’t like foreigners much, they do seem to have a soft spot for foreign cash. We have rules in this country about how our democracy works and everyone has to stick to them.”He added: “I think you see someone struggling to decide whether they’re really serious about trying to run for power or want to keep the protest going.”Get in touchContact Guardian Politics about this storyThe best public interest journalism relies on first-hand accounts from people in the know.
