So it starts with Fred and there’s only so much you can say and push and shout from the mountaintop.Quick GuideItalian F1 GP resultsShow1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes1:51:15.281 –25pts2George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes+3.875 –18pts3Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull+14.718 –15pts4Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren+19.056 –12pts5Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren+19.253 –10pts6Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari+24.655 –8pts7Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine+27.351 –6pts8Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls+45.136 –4pts9Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine+47.353 –2pts10Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls+58.187–1pt11Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi+65.18712Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi+66.18713Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams+74.11714Liam Lawson🇳🇿Red Bull+75.60915Oliver Bearman🇬🇧Haas+78.95816Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas+1 lap17Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams+1 lap18Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac+1 lap19Valtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac+2 lapsNCLance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinDNFNCFernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston MartinDNFNCCharles Leclerc🇲🇨FerrariDNFWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“I’ve already said that we had to look at how we communicate because if we continue to travel the same path, we’ll get the same result.”Leclerc is now 112 points behind Antonelli and Vasseur intimated that the team would now consider ­prioritising Hamilton.“The outcome of [turns] one-two is not good for the team,” Vasseur said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If we have a team order or ­whatever? I think that the good comparison that I made was that last year, [Oscar] Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season and if McLaren had put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion.“At one stage you have to take a decision but I think it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Now, we have time to discuss with the guys.”The discussion will have to be swift with the next round in Madrid next weekend but Hamilton was emphatic that Ferrari had to address the issues and once more compared the ­Scuderia’s operational activities unfavourably with his former team, the championship leaders Mercedes.“When I was at Mercedes we had written rules of engagement. And we never really had it too bad,” he said. “There was a moment with me and Nico [­Rosberg] a couple of times but more often than not, it was good. Here there are no rules. That’s something that needs to probably change.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘What are we doing?’: Brennan’s anger at racing in 44C heat as Van Aert wins shortened stage | Vuelta a España | The Guardian
description: Britain’s Matthew Brennan complained of the high temperatures the riders were racing in as Wout van Aert won stage 15 of the Vuelta a España
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: Britain’s Matthew Brennan complained of the high temperatures the riders were racing in as Wout van Aert won stage 15 of the Vuelta a España
Content: Wout van Aert celebrates after winning the 15th stage of the Vuelta a España from Palma del Rio to Córdoba.Photograph: Javier Lizón/EPAView image in fullscreenWout van Aert celebrates after winning the 15th stage of the Vuelta a España from Palma del Rio to Córdoba.Photograph: Javier Lizón/EPAVuelta a España‘What are we doing?’: Brennan’s anger at racing in 44C heat as Van Aert wins shortened stage‘It wouldn’t surprise me if some got heatstroke’Spain’s Enric Mas retains leader’s red jerseyJeremy Whittleand agenciesSun 6 Sep 2026 13.22 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 14.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBritain’s Matthew Brennan expressed his disbelief at the extreme heat riders had to endure on Sunday during stage 15 of theVuelta a España. His Visma Lease a Bike teammate Wout van Aert took a sprint win in Córdoba after the stage was shortened because of high temperatures.“It’s 41 degrees average,” Brennan said. “When I was on the climb at the start it was 44, and at that point you start thinking: ‘What are we doing?’ A normal office person has to have the temperature set at 20 degrees or whatever, and I’m sure that the UCI [cycling’s governing body] office will have their 20 as well.”Tim Wellens pulls away on last stage to win Tour of BritainRead moreThe medium mountain stage from Palma del Rio to Córdoba was originally scheduled to cover 189.7km, but organisers removed 79.5km from the middle ⁠of the route on Saturday afteractivating the extreme weather ​protocolfollowing ​several days of severe ​heat.Brennan said: “It’s not great, but we do it, and that’s the show we put on. But it wouldn’t surprise me if there were a few bodies coming home tonight with heatstroke.”Van Aert claimed his second victory ⁠in three stages after winning a five-rider sprint. The Belgian covered ⁠every attack from his four breakaway companions in the closing kilometres before producing a late ⁠surge just before the finish line to beat Alessandro ​Romele, of XDS Astana, ‌and Lidl-Trek’s Thibau ‌Nys.View image in fullscreenOscar Onley, of the Netcompany Ineos Cycling team, cools down after racing in stage 15’s extreme heat.Photograph: Tim de Waele/Getty Images“We tried to surprise the bunch by controlling the ‌whole day. We were still there with a few strong guys, and I knew people would not expect the attack. I smelled the moment on the intermediate sprint and with Matthew [Brennan] behind there was no ‌risk to try,” Van Aert said. “We always had a good option in the bunch. That’s ​how I like to race.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe race leader Enric Mas and his main ​general classification rivals ‌finished together ​after Movistar ​controlled the chase behind the decisive breakaway and Mas will carry the red jersey into the second rest day on Monday.Explore more on these topicsVuelta a EspañaCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carlos Alcaraz takes it up a level as he reaches US Open quarter-final | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: The reigning champion beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to move into the last eight at Flushing Meadows
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: The reigning champion beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to move into the last eight at Flushing Meadows
Content: Carlos Alcaraz said Flushing Meadows was special to him.Photograph: Cristóbal Herrera/EPAView image in fullscreenCarlos Alcaraz said Flushing Meadows was special to him.Photograph: Cristóbal Herrera/EPAUS Open Tennis 2026Carlos Alcaraz takes it up a level as he reaches US Open quarter-finalReigning champion beats Tommy Paul in straight setsSabalenka and Noskova to clash in last eightTumaini Carayolat Flushing MeadowsSun 6 Sep 2026 16.16 EDTFirst published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 16.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe straightforward scoreline at the end of Carlos Alcaraz’s third-round win over Wu Yibing did not quite reflect the Spaniard’s slight irritation with one aspect of his game. Alcaraz felt he had missed a few too many forehands, and almost immediately after departing Arthur Ashe Stadium, he reappeared on the practice court pounding forehands in the afternoon heat.Two days later, the extra care Alcaraz put into his game was reflected in a statement performance driven by his peerless forehand as he rose to the occasion in the biggest challenge of his comeback so far, dismantling the 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to continue his title defence by returning to the quarter-finals of the US Open.Dane Sweeny’s ‘career-changing’ US Open comes to an end – along with Australia’s singles hopesRead moreComing into the fourth round, things had progressed about as well as Alcaraz could have hoped. He had been efficient, clean and, most of all, he was striking the ball with total freedom after months of being unable to even use his wrist. The level the 23-year-old displayed on Sunday and the ease with which he dispatched such a high-quality opponent in Paul, however, took him to another level in his comeback.Afterwards, Paul spoke candidly about how vast the gap felt between himself and the seven-time grand slam champion. “It sucks, you know?” he said. “It felt like he’s playing at a completely different level than me, which is, like I said in the beginning, I could have played a lot better and still lost that match.“I was talking to my team right after the match. It sucks, because you feel like, ‘shit, it’s tough to win these matches against him.’ But at the same time, you learn a lot every time you play him.”There was plenty of doubt surrounding Alcaraz’s readiness to compete for the title considering he was returning at a major event in the best-of-five-sets format after a four-and-a-half-month layoff due to his wrist injury.His level serves as a message to the rest of the field that will not go unheard, one that he also shared in his on-court interview: “Except one year since 2021, I made at least the quarter-finals here,” Alcaraz said. “That means how special this place is to me, how good I’m playing every time I come here. I’m just trying to enjoy my time on the court.“So it probably doesn’t matter that I was out for four months and a half. Every time that I come here, I play my best.”Despite how well things had progressed, Alcaraz has had some creases to iron out in his game after so much time away.He started the tournament struggling with his serve, which was slower, inconsistent and imprecise. His serve has improved with each round in speed and precision.Considering the standards he has set for so much of his young career, it is hard to imagine that rate of improvement will not continue as the tournament endures.“Carlos is different, I guess,” said Paul. “It’s impressive to take time off like that and come back and feel, play as good as he has. I wouldn’t be able to do it, for sure.”Meanwhile, Aryna Sabalenka’s title defence at the US Open continued to gather steam as she returned to the quarter-finals with a solid performance and an assured victory, defeating Taylor Townsend of the United States 6-4, 6-3.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis was a challenging match despite the routine scoreline, with Sabalenka initially failing to serve out the first set, trailing 1-3 in set two and dropping serve four times.View image in fullscreenAryna Sabalenka will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the quarter-final.Photograph: Heather Khalifa/APHowever, she handled the decisive moments well, rolling through the final five games of the match to advance.“I love matches like that, because it was really challenging, and going through tough challenges and overcoming those challenges, it definitely gives you strength and really strong belief that you can do it,” said Sabalenka. “So these kind of matches is really like a boost of confidence.”A far greater challenge awaits Sabalenka in the quarter-final as she faces the Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova, who appears to be finding her feet again as she continues to digest her life-changing triumph in July.Noskova held her nerve at the end of one of the most spectacular contests of the tournament, recovering after squandering double match point at 5-4 in set two before clinching her sixth match point to close out against the 11th seed, Marta Kostyuk, 7-5, 5-7, 6-4.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026Carlos AlcarazAryna SabalenkaUS Open tennisTennisUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Canadian skyrunner goes missing during training session for Matterhorn record attempt | Extreme sports | The Guardian
description: Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during preparations for a record attempt in the Alps
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during preparations for a record attempt in the Alps
Content: Kalie McCrystal was last seen on the Italian side of the Matterhorn.Photograph: James Balog/Earth Vision InstituteView image in fullscreenKalie McCrystal was last seen on the Italian side of the Matterhorn.Photograph: James Balog/Earth Vision InstituteExtreme sportsCanadian skyrunner goes missing during training session for Matterhorn record attemptKalie McCrystal was hoping to break record in AlpsAthlete was last seen on Tuesday afternoonGuardian sportSun 6 Sep 2026 08.05 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 08.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCanadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during preparations for a record attempt in the Alps.McCrystal, from Squamish in British Columbia, was on a “reconnaissance/training session” in the run-up to her attempt at ascending and descending the 14,692 ft (4,478m) Matterhorn on the Swiss-Italian border.According to the Skyrunner World Series, the 38-year-old was last seen on Tuesday after she had reached the Matterhorn’s summit and was descending the Italian side of the mountain. The last sighting of the athlete was near a shelter at an altitude of around 12,500 ft.“There has been no further contact with her, and no one has seen or heard from her since,” the Skyrunner World Series said in the press release.Skyrunninginvolves running and scrambling at altitudes higher than 6,600ft. McCrystal was hoping to ascend and descend the Matterhorn in less than five hours during her record attempt.A helicopter search for McCrystal was called off on Friday after rescuers could find no trace of the athlete.McCrystal has climbed the Matterhorn before and, according to the Skyrunner World Series, she had “many years of experience in high-altitude and technical mountain terrain”.A friend of McCrystal said he did not believe the athlete had taken unnecessary risks before she went missing.“I know that this objective was well within her capabilities,” Duncan O’Regan, McCrystal’s friend and fellow mountain runner,told CBC. “She’s done much more difficult things, and this is not something that is beyond her capabilities. She’s comfortable in this terrain.”McCrystal has set several skyrunning records in Canada andEuropeand is a lawyer and staff member at Capilano University in North Vancouver.“Our thoughts are with Kalie’s family, friends and colleagues, and with everyone involved in the search efforts during this incredibly difficult time,” said Jason Dewling, the university’s president and vice-chancellor.Explore more on these topicsExtreme sportsUltrarunningCanadaSwitzerlandItalyEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: Roger Goodell’s NFL reign to reach 24 years after new contract extension | NFL | The Guardian
description: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has agreed on a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 league season, ending on 31 March 2031
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has agreed on a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 league season, ending on 31 March 2031
Content: Roger Goodell has been with the NFL for more than 40 years.Photograph: Richard Drew/APView image in fullscreenRoger Goodell has been with the NFL for more than 40 years.Photograph: Richard Drew/APNFLRoger Goodell’s NFL reign to reach 24 years after new contract extensionNFL owners approve deal for league commissionerRevenues and team values have soared under leadershipAssociated PressSun 6 Sep 2026 14.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNFL commissioner Roger Goodell has agreed on a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 league season, ending on 31 March 2031.In a memo sent to NFL owners on Sunday, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said: “We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.”Kraft is the chairman of the league’s compensation committee.Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard BryantRead more“Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success,” Kraft said. “To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee.”Financial terms of Goodell’s new contract weren’t immediately known. He reportedly earned $63.9m for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 seasons. The NFL hasn’t been required to disclose Goodell’s compensation on an annual basis because the league office is no longer structured as a tax-exempt trade association.This is the fifth contract extension for the 67-year-old Goodell, who has served as commissioner since succeeding Paul Tagliabue in 2006. He began his NFL career as an administrative intern in 1982 under then-commissioner Pete Rozelle.Under Goodell’s leadership, the NFL’s popularity and revenue have skyrocketed. The Washington Commanders were sold for $6.05bn in 2023 and the Seattle Seahawks were sold for $9.612bn this offseason, setting a new record.The league has continued expanding its global reach, and is playing a record nine international games this season.The expiration of Goodell’s contract coincides with the end of the current collective bargaining agreement, which also expires in March 2031.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan welcomes LeBron James to Philly after scoring: MLS roundup | MLS | The Guardian
description: The teenager welcomed LeBron James to the 76ers after another goal, while Vincent Janssen finally gave the Portland Timbers an MLS hat-trick
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The teenager welcomed LeBron James to the 76ers after another goal, while Vincent Janssen finally gave the Portland Timbers an MLS hat-trick
Content: Cavan Sullivan set another record for teenage goal-scoring in the Union’s win.Photograph: Isaiah Vazquez/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCavan Sullivan set another record for teenage goal-scoring in the Union’s win.Photograph: Isaiah Vazquez/Getty ImagesMLS16-year-old Cavan Sullivan welcomes LeBron James to Philly after scoring: MLS roundupTeenager welcomes LeBron to 76ersVincent Janssen scores Timbers’ first MLS hat-trickEmbolo scores, Messi assists in charged matchAgenciesSun 6 Sep 2026 13.35 EDTFirst published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 12.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePhiladelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history ⁠to record a five-match goal contribution streak on Saturday.At 16 years and 342 ⁠days old, ⁠Sullivan ​scored in his third consecutiveMLSmatch on Saturday when he tallied in the ⁠75th minute of the Union’s 2-0 victory over CF Montreal. He has three goals and ⁠three assists during his past five league matches.Sullivan’s 11 ​goal contributions (four goals, seven ‌assists) on ‌the season are the most ever by a 16-year-old in ‌MLS history, eclipsing the mark set by Freddy Adu (four goals, six assists) in 2005.So how did Sullivan celebrate his accomplishment? Well, by mimickingthe newest superstar in Philadelphia, LeBron James, with the latter’s ‌chalk toss.“I was waiting to do that for a while,” Sullivan said of the ​celebration. “I had Kim, our photographer, holding the chalk for multiple games. I just kept missing out on it! Tonight, great crowd, I figured it was the perfect ⁠time.”Sullivan became the youngest player to debut in ​North American ​team sports history when he ​made his league debut against the ​New England Revolution ‌on 17 July 2024. ​He was 14 years and 293 days old at the time, surpassing the mark set by Adu (14 years, 306 days). Adu set it for DC United in 2004.Vincent Janssen nets first hat-trick in Timbers history as Portland wins 5-4 thrillerVincent Janssen recorded the first regular-season hat-trick in the Portland Timbers’ MLS history to fuel a high-octane 5-4 victory over visiting ⁠Minnesota United on Saturday night.Janssen scored in the 11th, 26th and 55th minutes in his first start for Portland. His final goal gave the Timbers ⁠the lead for ⁠good. Janssen, ‌a Dutchman, was playing in his fourth match for the Timbers since being acquired via transfer from Belgian club Royal Antwerp in late July.Josh Sargent nets hat-trick as Robert Lewandowski scores in Toronto FC and Chicago’s high-scoring drawView image in fullscreenJosh Sargent netted a hat-trick in a 4-4 draw.Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty ImagesToronto FC and the visiting Chicago Fire fought to a 4-4 draw on Saturday night.Haitian international Derrick Etienne Jr tied ⁠the action-packed affair for Toronto in second-half stoppage time with a curling shot from the edge of the box.Josh Sargent scored a ⁠hat-trick for Toronto, ​while Maren Haile-Selassie scored twice for the Fire, giving him four goals in his past three MLS matches. Robert Lewandowski ⁠contributed a goal and an assist for Chicago, while Djordje Mihailovic tallied two assists for Toronto.Noah Allen and Johan Gomez made their Chicago debuts, as did Lewis Morgan for Toronto. Pereira, meanwhile, made his first start for Toronto since April. Both teams extended their unbeaten runs to six in MLS play.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHaile-Selassie opened the scoring by retrieving the ball off a ⁠corner kick and blasting it in from just outside the box in the 13th minute. ​Toronto goalkeeper Luka Gavran made an acrobatic ‌save off Philip Zinckernagel ‌to force the corner.Toronto’s designated players linked up for a speedy equalizer, Mihailovic feeding Sargent with a brilliantly placed ball over the top. TFC’s record signing sent Jack Elliott tumbling to the turf with a clever touch off his chest and blasted it past Brady in the ‌27th minute.Sargent scored again after a failed Fire clearance in the 38th minute. The ball ricocheted off two defenders and fell into his ​path before he put Toronto ahead 2-1. He bagged his ⁠hat-trick in the 54th minute with a low, powerful attempt in ​the corner of goal ​to make it 3-2.Lewandowski put the ‌Fire ahead in ​the 63rd minute ​after Haile-Selassie cleverly allowed Zinckernagel’s cross to run through to the Polish star.Breel Embolo scores, Messi assists as Atlanta United and Inter Miami drawLionel Messi’s international retirement serves as a reminder: watch him while you still canRead moreBreel Embolo converted a penalty kick in the 87th minute of his MLS debut to liftAtlanta Unitedto a ⁠2-2 draw against host Inter Miami on Saturday night.Embolo, the Switzerland national team star Atlanta signed in late August, was tripped ⁠in the penalty ⁠box with ​time dwindling. Fourteen minutes after teammate Miguel Almirón could not convert a penalty, Embolo calmly delivered a goal inside the right post ⁠past Miami’s Dayne St Clair.Embolo also had a look at a game-winner during stoppage time but missed high.Lionel Messi had one assist but was held scoreless one ‌game after his first four-goal performance in MLS. He took consecutive attempts on net in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage, but the first was saved and the second deflected out of bounds by Junior Alonso.Explore more on these topicsMLSPhiladelphia UnionUS sportsInter MiamiAtlanta UnitedPortland TimbersToronto FCShareReuse this content

title: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea
Content: Arsenal's manager, Mikel Arteta, makes his point to his captain, Martin Ødegaard during their win over Chelsea.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APView image in fullscreenArsenal's manager, Mikel Arteta, makes his point to his captain, Martin Ødegaard during their win over Chelsea.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APArsenal‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to comeManager delighted by reaction to Chelsea’s openerAlonso says his side must be ‘tighter’Jacob Steinbergat the Emirates StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 15.52 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 18.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after thePremier Leaguechampions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday.Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season whenMorgan Rogersstruck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over ChelseaRead more“It was an exceptional performance,” Arteta said. “I enjoyed every minute from beginning to end, and the beginning was tough. But the team responded in a spectacular way – the conviction, the determination, the quality. It was beautiful. It was a fascinating game.“I think it’s an indication for us of how we are capable of ­performing at an even higher level than last ­season. It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team. We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer. This is the ambition of the team.”Arsenal and City are the only sides who have won their first three games, a statistic Arteta took as evidence that the league will be even harder this time. “It is going to be super hard, the margins you win games,” he said.“We went to Villa Park a few days ago and it was really tough. Today again. We’ll go to Sunderland and it’ll again be so, so tough. We know every week is going to be like this but that’s what we prepare for.”Arteta was delighted with an exceptional midfield display from Ødegaard. Arsenal’s captain looks fit after two years of injury problems and has started the campaign with three goals in four games.“He feels, confidence-wise, I think one of the highest that I’ve seen him,” Arteta said of the Norwegian. “He has a point to prove from last season as well, missing so much football. Kai is the same. I don’t know how many times they played together in the last three years but probably not much. He is enjoying his football. He was running ­forward, having shots, creating for his teammates.”Arteta, who hopes Cristhian ­Mosquera will make a swift recovery from a muscle problem, was similarly positive about Havertz after the ­German impressed against his old club. “He looks settled, he looks happy, in his personal life some great things have happened,” he said. “He looks fit, he looks happy and he is scoring goals.”View image in fullscreenKai Havertz (right) celebrates scoring Arsenal’s first goal with Christos Tzolis and Gabriel.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersWhile Arsenal celebrated, ­Chelsea reflected on coming up short. The Blues were exciting in attack but defensive shortcomings led to their first defeat underXabi Alonso, whose new team have conceded seven in their first three league games.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“My priority is to win games and it’s easier when you don’t concede many,” Alonso said. “This is something that we need to address. We want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.“We wanted to compete, we came to win. We were not that far, but it went their way. We could have scored to make it 2-1 and you never know what happens. But the result is the result, I’m not fighting against that. It hurts. But this is the first defeat, it is going to be a long journey and it doesn’t have a big impact in our mood.”Chelsea are without a clean sheet in their past 19 league games but Alonso did not want to park the bus. “I want to compete in the best possible way to win,” he said. “Today we didn’t want to sit deep from the first minute and to wait and to make a long game. We wanted to be active, we wanted to be protagonists in the pressing, sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower, to have good possessions. And we have done many right things. We need to make it better.”Alonso was optimistic that Moisés Caicedo is not enduring a long-term issue after the midfielder missed out with injury. Caicedo is yet to start this season and it is uncertain if he will be back for Chelsea’s Carabao Cup tie against Leeds on Wednesday.“It’s about assessing the risk,” Alonso said. “Probably last week we took him on too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalMikel ArtetaChelseaXabi AlonsoPremier LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw | Everton | The Guardian
description: The manager, praising Everton’s resilience after securing a late 2-2 draw with Manchester United, said: ‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: The manager, praising Everton’s resilience after securing a late 2-2 draw with Manchester United, said: ‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’
Content: David Moyes said Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester United was a ‘brilliant goal, brilliant technique’.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAView image in fullscreenDavid Moyes said Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester United was a ‘brilliant goal, brilliant technique’.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAEverton‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United drawManager praises team’s resilience after late equaliser‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’Andy Hunterat Hill Dickinson StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 14.49 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 15.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDavid Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind tosalvage a point against Manchester Unitedthrough Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.Maitland-Niles stunner rescues late point for Everton against Manchester UnitedRead moreTyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If nobody knew you that goal would get you plenty of headlines,” he said of Maitland-Niles, a £4.3m deadline-day signing from Lyon. “It was a brilliant goal, brilliant technique. We have not had a chance to get to know Ainsley but it was a great start from him.”Explore more on these topicsEvertonDavid MoyesManchester UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia | European club football | The Guardian
description: Fermín, Raphinha and Pedri also score to keep 100% record
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Fermín, Raphinha and Pedri also score to keep 100% record
Content: Lamine Yamal silences the Mestalla by giving Barcelona the lead after only six minutes.Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLamine Yamal silences the Mestalla by giving Barcelona the lead after only six minutes.Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesEuropean club footballEuropean football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of ValenciaGatti’s stoppage-time header rescues Juve against MilanGoalkeeper Koeman Jr scores two penalties in EredivisieAgenciesSun 6 Sep 2026 17.25 EDTFirst published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 14.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLamine Yamal struck twice forBarcelonaas they demolishedValencia5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’sReal Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betison Friday. Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.European football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten InterRead moreBarcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Fermín dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star. Fermín netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after the former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up. Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric García had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with teammate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start sincearriving this summer from Manchester City.Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Fermín fed him. The Valencia goalkeeper, Stole Dimitrievski, saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo. Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barça debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide. Lamine Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barça’s fifth.In Serie A, Ruben Amorim’sMilanwere pegged back by a 92nd-minute equaliser fromJuventusin a 1-1 draw in Turin on Sunday. Teenage sensation Alphadjo Cisse had given Milan the lead but the Juve centre-back Federico Gatti came off the bench to head home and earn a share of the spoils in stoppage time.Milan took the lead on 69 minutes ⁠with a superb finish from Cisse, who controlled Samuel Chukwueze’s crossfield pass with a deft touch in the box. The 19-year-old showed quick feet to create space to shoot ⁠and fired the ball low into the far corner, adding to his debut goal away ​at Torino on the opening day. But the visitors could not ‌hold on and when Teun Koopmeiners delivered a cross from the left, Gatti rose highest to score ‌with a powerful header.View image in fullscreenJuventus’s Federico Gatti takes the acclaim of the Turin crowd after levelling against Milan at the death.Photograph: Marco Alpozzi/LaPresse/APThe ⁠draw leaves both sides ⁠on seven points ​from their opening three games, with Milan fourth on the table, ahead of fifth-placed Juve on goals scored.Giorgi Kvernadze scored a winner seven minutes from the end to secure all three points forFrosinoneat home toVeneziaafter the latter had rallied from two goals down but went home with nothing.Bolognatwice came from behind to secure a 2-2 draw at home toSassuolo, a game that ended with the hosts’ head coach Domenico Tedesco receiving a red card. Artem Dovbyk netted his first goal for the ​home side to equalise in stoppage time.The English 19-year-old Jay Robinson gaveMonzaa 1-0 lead in the first half atParma, but 18-year-old Simone Lontani equalised on the hour-mark, with the game finishing 1-1. For both players it was their firstSerie Agoals, and for both clubs their first point of the campaign. Forward Robinson is on loan at Monza from Southampton.Meanwhile, Ronald Koeman Jr, the goalkeeper son of the former Netherlands player and manager Ronald Koeman, scored two penalties for Dutch sideTelstarto rescue a point in theirEredivisiematch withCambuur. His second spot-kick was converted in the 11th minute of added time.Koeman Jr, 31, converted his first penalty on 63 minutes before his ice-cool equaliser. He previously scored from the spot at the end of last season to ensure his side avoided relegation from the Dutch top flight.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenTelstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr is hugged by a teammate after his late penalty rescued a point.Photograph: ANP/ShutterstockIn Germany,Mainzignited their Bundesliga season with a thumping 5-0 win over haplessHamburg, whileAugsburgclimbed ⁠to the top of the table following a 4-1 win atEintracht Frankfurton Sunday.Mainz took the lead on 19 minutes as Sheraldo Becker was played in on goal by ⁠Kaishu Sano and picked out the bottom corner. Becker then turned provider as his low cross was converted at the back post by Phillipp Mwene for ⁠a 2-0 half-time lead.Becker was again involved with the next goal as he set up ​Phillip Tietz to bundle the ball home. Tietz ‌then added a fourth ‌as he beat Heuer Fernandes, before Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer punished his former employers ‌with a fifth.Augsburg have a haul of six points following ​their excellent win at Frankfurt, where they had to come from behind, having trailed 1-0 at half-time. Jonathan Burkardt headed the home side in front inside six minutes.Arijon Ibrahimovic ​headed in at the back post ​on debut inside the first minute of the re-start for the equaliser. Within a minute, ‌Augsburg were 2-1 ahead ​as the ball ​fell to Robin Fellhauer in the box and he converted to turn the game on its head. Alexis Claude-Maurice and Fabian Rieder added further goalsAugsburg lead theBundesligaon goal difference ahead of Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and Elversberg, who all have two wins from two.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballBarcelonaValenciaLa LigaAugsburgMainz 05HamburgnewsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning start | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Khadija Shaw scored twice as Manchester City began the defence of the Women’s Super League title with a 3-1 win against Birmingham
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Khadija Shaw scored twice as Manchester City began the defence of the Women’s Super League title with a 3-1 win against Birmingham
Content: Khadija Shaw shows her delight after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw shows her delight after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWomen’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning startStriker scores twice to sink BirminghamArsenal, Palace, Spurs and Liverpool winTom Garryat the Joie StadiumSun 6 Sep 2026 14.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSome things just feel inevitable. Some strikers just feel inevitable. Despite a new season, a fresh start and new opponents, it is still the same storyline forManchester City: Khadija Shaw wins them the game. The Jamaica striker began the campaign exactly how she finished the previous league season, with two goals, and demonstrated why it was so crucial that the club eventually persuaded her to sign a new contract in the summer.Last season’s Golden Boot winner in the Women’s Super League could have scored at least twice in the first half had it not been for an excellent debut performance from Sophie Baggaley in goal for promotedBirmingham.Brighton 0-1 Arsenal: Women’s Super League – as it happenedRead moreShaw, though, was not to be denied and she rose highest to head in twice from second-half corners, taken first by Kerstin Casparij and then by the debutant Beth Mead, to score her side’s second and third goals in a 3-1 victory. By then, Mary Fowler’s low finish had already opened the scoring with Manchester City’s 1,000th goal as a professional women’s side.Birmingham grabbed a late consolation goal through Océane Hurtré, who capitalised on a defensive lapse from Jade Rose and rolled the ball home in the 90th minute, and there were plenty of encouraging signs overall for the second-tier champions of last season.Quick GuidePalace face scrutiny over substitutionsShowCrystal Palace could face a points deduction or potentially be forced to replay their game against Everton on Sunday, which Palace won 1-0, after it emerged that the hosts breached the rules around substitutions by making changes at four separate moments in the second half of the Women's Super League match.The WSL, Pro Ref and both clubs have all launched investigations into the incident. The newly promoted Palace brought on Kirsty Howat to replace Shannon O'Brien in the 97th minute, having already made three previous substitutions across three separate second-half opportunities.A WSL spokesperson said: "We can confirm there was a breach of competition rules in the Crystal Palace versus Everton match. Crystal Palace used a fourth substitution opportunity during a fourth stoppage in play, when the rules permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match. We will now conduct an investigation alongside both clubs and Pro Ref and update in due course."Jo Potter's side were already leading the match thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith's 34th-minute opener. There were eight minutes of stoppage time indicated for the end of the second half, so the  substitution in question came with merely seconds remaining. The consequences could be significant for Palace, depending on the outcome of the investigation and the verdict of any potential tribunal.The WSL's rules regarding the fielding of an ineligible player list the potential punishments in rule 7.13.2, which include the possibility that the points gained from the match be deducted or that the match be replayed. It is understood that the team of match officials who worked on that Palace-Everton game will not be appointed to the next round of games in WSL/ WSL2 on the weekend of 12-13 September, in light of this incident.Teams are permitted to use no more than three substitution opportunities per match, in addition to being able to make replacements at half-time and for concussion substitutions.Tom GarryWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The Blues were playing on the same ground where they were relegated in 2022 after a 6-0 loss to City, but on Sunday Amy Merricks’s side look far more competitive than the Birmingham team that said goodbye to the top tier four seasons ago, having kept the scoreline goalless until after half-time.Nonetheless, on the day of Lauren Hemp’s 200th City appearance it was a dominant start from the defending champions, whose head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, said: “We created a lot of scoring chances. The first half [we were] a little bit hesitant on the ball, not determined with or without the ball, but the second half was better.”View image in fullscreenArsenal’s Lisa Baum fires in the only goal at Brighton.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersMerricks, who hailed Baggaley’s debut as “exceptional”, said: “We got into some good areas and lacked just a bit of anticipation that we would get there. That’s just down to belief, that’s not quality. I’m really pleased with the performance. I’m disappointed with the result but really pleased with the platform we’ve given ourselves to build on.”Earlier, Lisa Baum marked herArsenaldebut with an exquisitely taken goal and her early strike was enough to secure a 1-0 victory atBrightonand inflict a defeat on their new head coach, Arturo Ruiz. The 19‑year‑old Germany youth international created room to shoot inside the area in the 10th minute and rifled home a clinical finish from a tight angle, in off the underside of the crossbar, to make an immediate impression on the delighted, travelling Arsenal fans behind that goal.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBaum, who arrived this summer from RB Leipzig, was one of four new signings to start the game for Arsenal, alongside Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez. Arsenal had failed to win at Brighton in the past two league campaigns and will have been very satisfied to open their title bid with a victory as they seek to hunt down a first league title since 2019. Ruiz, who has been in charge at Brighton for nine days, saw some encouraging signs from his new team with Kiko Seike and Fran Kirby both going close.It was a day for important debut goals as Lexi Lloyd-Smith slotted home on her first appearance forCrystal Palaceto give the promoted side a priceless 1-0 win againstEvertonto start their campaign. Another debutant quickly impressed atTottenhamas their new striker Kirsty Hanson scored twice to help them to beatWest Ham3-1.Liverpoolwere the day’s most emphatic winners as they cruised to a 4-0 win at promotedCharlton. The Germany striker Vivien Endemann scored on her debut for Liverpool after Grace Fisk had scored twice. Cornelia Kapocs added a stoppage‑time penalty to make it a poor start for Charlton, who did not register a shot on target and recorded just two efforts off target.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester City WomenBirmingham City WomenArsenal WomenWomen's footballBrighton & Hove Albion WomenCrystal Palace WomennewsShareReuse this content

title: Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-election | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, will be standing for re-election in March despite being under enormous pressure to resign
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, will be standing for re-election in March despite being under enormous pressure to resign
Content: Gianni Infantino has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAGianni InfantinoEmbattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-electionInfantino is under pressure to resign after sell-off planUefa has led calls for president to quitGuardian sportand agenciesSun 6 Sep 2026 10.03 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 15.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Fifa president,Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes inFifatournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.Uefa legal case may be beginning of the end for Infantino as Trump’s support evaporates | Barney RonayRead moreUefa, the European governing body,has led callsfor Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.But for the first time since the plan became public, Fifa has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031.A Fifa spokesperson said: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino. Montagliani,a Fifa vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed Fifa’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.However, Infantino is not without friends – Saudi Arabia, the 2034 men’s World Cup hosts, came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body, Caf, and South America’s Conmebol also supportive.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAs the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to Fifa to extend his term of office, which began in 2016. Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by 18 November.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaUefaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw | Championship | The Guardian
description: Wolves took the lead twice but Birmingham grabbed a point in the 2-2 draw thanks to Jackson Tchatchoua’s shocking own goal
Author: Peter Lansley
Headline: Wolves took the lead twice but Birmingham grabbed a point in the 2-2 draw thanks to Jackson Tchatchoua’s shocking own goal
Content: Wolves’ Jackson Tchatchoua endures the taunts of Birmingham fans after his own goal made it 2-2.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAView image in fullscreenWolves’ Jackson Tchatchoua endures the taunts of Birmingham fans after his own goal made it 2-2.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAChampionshipArmstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves drawPeter Lansleyat St Andrew'sSun 6 Sep 2026 09.40 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIf only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance in the 87th minute, had shot into the same corner of the net at the Railway End that his teammate ­Jackson Tchatchoua had located when scoring one of the most ­memorable own goals at the end of the first half, then César Peixoto’s team would surely now be second in theChampionship.Instead Armstrong, one of the Football League’s most proven goalscorers, lifted his shot over an open goal from 10 yards when played in by Fer López at the end of this implausibly open derby. Birmingham ultimately deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season.Championship roundup: Bristol City add to Burnley’s woes, West Ham beat DerbyRead moreAfter their4-2 defeat at West Hamon Tuesday, Wolves look as vulnerable defensively as they can be devas­tating going forward. Only Burnley, relegated with them last season, have conceded more than their 10 goals.Tom Wagner, the ­Birmingham chair, was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in February and was treated to a thrilling game. Spoils were shared but Chris Davies was happy with his side after they twice came from behind. “I’ll always be content when the players put in that heart and spirit,” the ­Birmingham manager said. “When you look at the quality of their team, I’ll be astonished if they’re not in the top four. Second half, we put them to the sword.”López scored in the third ­minute for Wolves and, after Jay ­Stansfield equalised in controversial circum­stances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again. But then came the moment that could haunt ­Tchatchoua. The Cameroon right‑back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his ­goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sá into his own goal.That moment set the tempo for the rest of a game. Wolves, despite ­retaining the majority of their ­Premier League squad after the transfer deadline, know sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.View image in fullscreenAdam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAPeixoto called for video assistant referees to be brought in to the Championship after Stansfield appeared to handle when bringing down Patrick Roberts’s brilliant chip before hammering home Birmingham’s first equaliser. “If the referee doesn’t see it, then what can you do?” Stansfield said.Peixoto said: “I don’t know why they don’t have VAR in the Champion­ship. It’s very important to help the refe­rees to take the best decisions. I saw a handball and in the screen we saw a handball.” The ­Portuguese coach also confirmed that in a pre‑season meeting with Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), ­managers were told that grappling at corners would be penalised. “But it’s not happening,” he said.While the home side dominated the second half, Wolves could have put the game to bed before Birmingham got going. López was involved in the buildup before advancing to side‑foot home Rodrigo Gomes’s right‑wing cross to the near post for his third goal of the season.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Then in the 19th minute, ­Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Raúl ­Jiménez to steal the ball and put in Gomes who allowed James ­Beadle to save his dinked attempt.Krejci is one of the elite players surprisingly still at Wolves. The Czechia captain’s bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves another endorphin boost. It was short-lived, however, as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragicomic own goal. Jiménez hit the crossbar, as he did in defeat at West Ham, but then Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.Wolves had the clearest of many chances both teams had to win the game. López dispossessed Demarai Gray inside the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, squared for ­Armstrong. Somehow he contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal. “The way Jack[son Tchatchoua] committed his mistake, Adam committed the mistake in the opposite side,” Peixoto said. “We have to take the confidence to them and keep fighting and work hard for the next game.”There was still time for ­Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced a free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá to show why he was awarded a new contract, as he tipped the ball aside to ensure this pulsating match finished even.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipBirmingham CityWolverhampton Wanderersmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers | Burnley | The Guardian
description: Vardy signed as a free agent after departing Cremonese in summer and plays on despite burgeoning media career
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Vardy signed as a free agent after departing Cremonese in summer and plays on despite burgeoning media career
Content: Jamie Vardy spent last season at Cremonese in Italy but became a free agent in the summer.Photograph: Riccardo Bortolotti/APView image in fullscreenJamie Vardy spent last season at Cremonese in Italy but became a free agent in the summer.Photograph: Riccardo Bortolotti/APBurnleyJamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglersVardy a free agent after departing CremonesePlans to play on despite burgeoning media careerJohn BrewinSun 6 Sep 2026 11.16 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 18.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in theChampionshipas a free agent.Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.Championship roundup: Bristol City add to Burnley’s woes, West Ham beat DerbyRead moreHis podcast,Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party, made the news last week for Mike Dean’slifting of the lidon his antics as a Premier League referee and has secured broadcast rights for a Bundesliga watch-along. He has also, with his wife Rebekah, starred in an ITV reality series, and been the subject of a Netflix documentary.Despite those wider interests, Vardy’s intention has been to carry on playing, having been a late starter, making his Football League debut at 25 after signing for Leicester.Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last term and, with Nicky Hayen as their manager, remain without a win after their opening five games of the Championship campaign, losing to Bristol City on Saturday. Vardy joins a team bottom of the division.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town,” Vardy said. “I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”In June, he said of Leicester, now in League One, currently struggling under the management of Russell Martin: “I think that’s gone. I’ll always support them, always follow them. I think that’s the best thing I can do now.”Explore more on these topicsBurnleyJamie VardyChampionshipnewsShareReuse this content

Author: Guardian staff reporter

Content: Richard Hughes (centre) will work with Al-Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenRichard Hughes (centre) will work with Al-Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAAl-HilalRichard Hughes confirmed as Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool departureHughes joins Saudi exodus after two years at AnfieldMartinelli, Summerville and Watkins are at Al-HilalReuters and Guardian sportSun 6 Sep 2026 17.15 EDTLast modified on Sun 6 Sep 2026 17.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRichard Hughes has been appointed as the sporting director ⁠of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club confirmed on ⁠Sunday, following ⁠his ​departure from Liverpool.Hughes, 47, joinedLiverpoolin 2024 from Bournemouth. ⁠He appointed Arne Slot as Jürgen Klopp’s successor as head coach, ⁠a decision that paid immediate dividends ​as the Reds ‌claimed the ‌Premier League title in 2024-25. title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren, while Rangers lost Lawrence Shankland to injury but Ryan Naderi scored in a 1-0 victory against Motherwell
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren, while Rangers lost Lawrence Shankland to injury but Ryan Naderi scored in a 1-0 victory against Motherwell
Content: Yang Hyun-jun slots home to put Celtic 2-1 ahead of St Mirren.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenYang Hyun-jun slots home to put Celtic 2-1 ahead of St Mirren.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St MirrenRangers beat Motherwell 1-0 but lose Shankland to injuryKerjota’s late winner sees Hearts edge past DundeePress AssociationSun 6 Sep 2026 16.25 EDTFirst published on Sat 5 Sep 2026 12.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleYang Hyun-jun scored the winner asCelticcame from behind to beat an impressiveSt Mirrenside 2-1.St Mirrenwere heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half.Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip toSt Johnstoneand two games against Rangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”Rangersstriker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal againstMotherwellat Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.Motherwell dominated possession and created several chances butRangerswere more effective in the final third and should have added to their lead. Kim Min-su missed a first-half penalty and the debutant striker Kevin Kelsy was among those to pass up good opportunities after he came off the bench.View image in fullscreenLawrence Shankland leaves the pitch unaided but his manager later revealed the club fear his hamstring injury is significant.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PARangers ultimately saw out the game without any late scares as they recorded a third consecutive Premiership victory.Of Shankland, the Rangers manager, Derek McInnes, said he fears the injury is similarly significant to the one that kept him out for two months early in 2026. McInnes said: “He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had atHeartslast January. We don’t want to speculate too much but he says it feels similar, in the same area, so we’ll get him scanned on Monday.“He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of, he just felt it pull up. It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games, and we’ve waited long and hard for that.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMichael Forbes scored an added-time equaliser forDundee UnitedagainstFalkirk, who had led at Tannadice thanks to Jacob Murrell’s fourth-minute opener, whileKilmarnockpicked up their first point but are still waiting for a first Premiership win of the season after a 0-0 draw atAberdeen. Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola was sent off for a second yellow card after 83 minutes but the hosts could not find a way past the 10 men.Sabah Kerjota scored a stoppage-time winner asHeartsstaged a dramatic late fightback to defeatDundee2-1 at Tynecastle and make it four Premiership victories in succession.The Jambos were frustrated for long periods after the Dark Blues took the lead in the 17th minute through Bradley Fink. But Hearts drew level in the 84th minute through a Claudio Braga penalty before Dundee had Zan Besir sent off as the match ticked into stoppage time.Wouter Vrancken’s buoyant side made their extra man count when Albanian substitute Kerjota drilled in his first goal since arriving at Tynecastle last summer in the sixth minute of added time. The victory elevated the Jambos, unbeaten in eight in all competitions, to second in the table.Josh Fowler’s first-half double securedSt Johnstonea 2-1 win overHibernianand moved them above their opponents in the table. Fowler netted from close range on 16 minutes, then slotted home a penalty after Nathan Lowe had levelled for Hibs to secure Saints’ second win of the campaign. The visitors were the better team in the second period but Simo Valakari’s team held on for a 2-1 success to move into seventh spot.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipCelticRangersMotherwellSt MirrenAberdeenKilmarnocknewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Premier League – as it happened | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Kai Havertz scored and made the winner for Martin Odegaard as Arsenal asserted their supremacy
Author: Rob Smyth
Headline: Kai Havertz scored and made the winner for Martin Odegaard as Arsenal asserted their supremacy
Content: 7h ago13.55 EDTDavid HytnerMatch report: Arsenal 2-1 ChelseaThe first heavyweight encounter of thePremier Leagueseason was previewed in some quarters as the immovable object versus the irresistible force. Arsenal do not give an inch. Chelsea have been fun and free-scoring under Xabi Alonso. Yet that overlooked something pretty fundamental. The percussive force of Arsenal’s game when they have the ball and want to make something happen.Chelsea landed a significant blow after 77 seconds when Morgan Rogers put them in front with nicely executed volley from the edge of the area. It was not only the first goal that Arsenal have conceded this season but one with rich narrative strands. Rogers was chased by Arsenal over the summer only to joinChelseafor £117m.The story here was about Arsenal’s reaction. The sheer fury of it. For a blistering spell that culminated in Kai Havertz’s equaliser on 25 minutes, they threatened to blow Chelsea off the pitch. Arsenal’s confidence shone through. They had not lost to their cross-town rivals in eleven previous meetings in all competitions, winning eight, but it was rooted in more than that. They had too much for Chelsea and they knew it.Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over ChelseaRead moreShare
